Treble & bass cheatsheet

Treble lines: E G B D F
Treble spaces: F A C E
Bass lines: G B D F A
Bass spaces: A C E G

Each line or space advances one letter. Middle C sits one ledger line below the treble staff and one ledger line above the bass staff.

Play the melody from notation

Play the highlighted note to start.

Reading strategy

Read left to right, one note at a time. Aim for accuracy first, then smooth playing. This exercise uses quarter notes at your own pace. Octave equivalents are accepted at beginner level.

Tap along with the metronome. First click is beat one.

Tap the button, press Space or strike a MIDI key. Feedback compares your taps with the nearest expected rhythmic subdivision. Audio begins after your first click.

Rhythm reference

Semibreve = 4 beats
Minim = 2 beats
Crotchet = 1 beat
Quaver = ½ beat
Semiquaver = ¼ beat

In 4/4, each bar contains four crotchet beats. Count subdivisions aloud: “1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and”.

Write music with your keyboard

Play notes on your MIDI keyboard to enter them on the staff, or use the on-screen keyboard. The app uses the metre sequence selected in Rhythm Lab and exports a standard MIDI file for Logic Pro. Every note is displayed. Select a note in the score or list to edit pitch, duration or delete it.

Composition tips

Start with C, D, E, G and A. Write a four-bar phrase using a mix of crotchets and minims. Then play it back and notice how pitch and duration work together.

0Notes written
MIDI export preserves pitch, timing and note length, but not engraving details such as clefs, slurs or articulation. Open it in Logic Pro's Score Editor to inspect the notation.

Hear a note, then find it

Listen, then play the note you heard.

Ear training

For a single note, reproduce the pitch. For an interval, reproduce both notes in order. A reference C4 is played before each challenge to develop relative pitch rather than pretending everyone has perfect pitch.

8-week intensive course

Daily practice • 30 minutes

Aim for five sessions a week. Eight weeks builds a solid foundation, not instant professional-level fluency. Prioritise accuracy, then speed.

How to learn sheet music with Notation Lab

Start with treble and bass clef note recognition, then read short melodies, practise rhythmic values and copy phrases in standard notation. The five mastery bars use your exercise results; opening a lesson does not award mastery.

Compound metres such as 6/8 and additive metres such as 2+2+3/8 help you practise different beat groupings. The eight-week course contains forty expandable steps. Read the complete practice guide.

Safari supports the virtual and computer keyboards. Physical MIDI requires a browser with Web MIDI support. Progress stays in this browser; use backup export and restore to transfer it.
